findings.title: Existing SQL parser/command tests will break against the stub DB
findings.body: `TablesList` now goes through the stub `DB.RunCommands`, which always returns "not implemented". `TablesList` therefore always fails, and `NewSQLCommand` always returns the `sql-invalid-sql` BadRequest. The existing tests that assert parsed table names and successful SQL command creation (in `pkg/expr/sql` parser tests and `pkg/expr` SQL command tests) were not updated or skipped in this PR, so CI will fail. Those tests should be skipped or rewritten to assert the new disabled behaviour.

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; the feature flag is silently dead
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` negates the `sqlExpressions` flag, then returns false in both branches. The flag lookup has no effect, and the function name suggests the flag still controls the feature. The `sqlExpressions` toggle is still registered and documented, so operators who enable it get "sqlExpressions is not implemented" with no hint that the flag was intentionally neutered. Replace this with a plain `return false` (or remove the check) plus a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264. Also mark the flag as deprecated or no-op in the registry and docs.

findings.title: Dead DuckDB code path left in place, including SQL string building and logging of raw user SQL
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds a hand-escaped `json_serialize_sql('%s')` command, which was the injection vector. On every call it now logs the full user SQL and the command at Error level, because the stub always fails. The variable is still named `duckDB`. Leaving the vulnerable command construction in place makes it easy to re-enable accidentally by swapping the DB implementation back. It also spams error logs on the `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path, which does not go through the reader's flag check. The function should return an error immediately.
